title: Why Do Onions Make You CRY? 🧅
description:
You're chopping an onion like a TV chef... and suddenly you're sobbing. Nobody died. It's an onion. Subscribe for a new strange question every day.

Every onion cell is a tiny booby trap: an enzyme kept in one compartment, sulfur compounds in another. Your knife smashes the wall, they mix, and a SECOND enzyme (only discovered in 2002) turns the result into a tear gas called syn-propanethial-S-oxide. It floats up, lands on your eyes and pings the nerve endings there, so your brain floods your eyes with tears to wash it out. You're not crying. You're rinsing.

And in 2025, high-speed cameras caught onions spraying tiny droplets up to 60 cm high. A blunt knife or fast chopping sprays more. So: sharp knife, slow cuts... or just let the onion win.
